 819    def _sweep_provider_scratch(
 820        self,
 821        run_dir: Path,
 822        resource_id: str,
 823        attempt_num: int,
 824        known_before: Set[str],
 825        attempts_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
 826        attempts_before: Optional[Set[str]] = None,
 827        owned_attempt_name: Optional[str] = None,
 828    ) -> List[str]:
 829        """Moves anything a provider left in the evidence namespace into scratch.
 830
 831        Providers write where they like -- they run in the repository with no
 832        filesystem sandbox -- so the boundary is enforced afterwards rather than
 833        assumed. Two escapes are swept: artifacts dropped at the run's evidence
 834        root (HOWLFRAM-SLOPFIX-05), and directories invented under
 835        `implementation/attempts/` that imitate a canonical attempt
 836        (HOWLFRAM-SLOPFIX-06, where `01-claude/` made a three-attempt run look
 837        like four). Both are relocated with provenance and nothing is deleted:
 838        the artifacts may well be useful, they are simply not evidence.
 839        """
 840        scratch = self._provider_scratch_dir(run_dir, attempt_num, resource_id)
 841        swept: List[str] = []
 842
 843        def relocate(entry: Path, label: str) -> None:
 844            scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 845            destination = scratch / entry.name
 846            if destination.exists():
 847                destination = scratch / f"{entry.name}.{attempt_num:02d}"
 848            try:
 849                entry.replace(destination)
 850            except OSError:
 851                return
 852            swept.append(label)
 853
 854        for entry in sorted(run_dir.iterdir()):
 855            if entry.name in known_before:
 856                continue
 857            if entry.name in CONTROL_PLANE_RUN_ARTIFACTS:
 858                continue
 859            relocate(entry, entry.name)
 860
 861        # A directory under attempts/ that this run did not create is a
 862        # provider's guess at its own attempt label, not an attempt.
 863        if attempts_dir is not None and attempts_dir.is_dir():
 864            known_attempts = attempts_before or set()
 865            for entry in sorted(attempts_dir.iterdir()):
 866                if not entry.is_dir():
 867                    continue
 868                if entry.name in known_attempts or entry.name == owned_attempt_name:
 869                    continue
 870                if (entry / "attempt_record.json").is_file():
 871                    # Real control-plane evidence; never touch it.
 872                    continue
 873                for child in sorted(entry.iterdir()):
 874                    relocate(child, f"implementation/attempts/{entry.name}/{child.name}")
 875                try:
 876                    # Only ever removes the empty shell left behind, so the
 877                    # canonical attempt count stops counting a fake one.
 878                    entry.rmdir()
 879                except OSError:
 880                    pass
 881
 882        if swept:
 883            atomic_write_json(
 884                scratch / "_provenance.json",
 885                {
 886                    "origin": "provider_scratch",
 887                    "created_by": resource_id,
 888                    "attempt": attempt_num,
 889                    "relocated_from": f".task_runs/{run_dir.name}/",
 890                    "files": swept,
 891                    "note": (
 892                        "Written by the provider inside the control plane's "
 893                        "evidence namespace and relocated here. Not control "
 894                        "plane evidence."
 895                    ),
 896                    "swept_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
 897                    "schema": PROVIDER_SCRATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 898                },
 899            )
 900            self._record_scratch_manifest(
 901                run_dir,
 902                run_dir.name,
 903                attempt_num,
 904                resource_id,
 905                scratch,
 906                status="relocated",
 907                artifacts=swept,
 908            )
 909        return swept
 910
 911    def _attach_terminal_disposition(
 912        self,
 913        attempt_record: Dict[str, Any],
 914        attempts_dir: Path,
 915        attempt_num: int,
 916        attempted: Set[str],
 917        task_spec: TaskSpec,
 918    ) -> None:
 919        """Records why a salvaged final attempt has no successor.
 920
 921        Attempts that hand off carry `rollback` and `next_selection`; the one
 922        that exhausts the budget carried neither, so "no provider remained" and
 923        "nobody wrote the field" looked identical in the evidence. The candidate
 924        is deliberately not rolled back -- it is parked for governance -- and
 925        that has to be stated, not inferred (HOWLFRAM-SLOPFIX-06).
 926        """
 927        remaining: List[str] = []
 928        pool = self.config.provider_pool
 929        if pool is not None:
 930            try:
 931                for resource_id in pool.select_candidates(
 932                    task_category="code_heavy", task=task_spec
 933                ):
 934                    if resource_id not in attempted:
 935                        remaining.append(resource_id)
 936            except Exception:
 937                remaining = []
 938
 939        attempt_record["max_attempts"] = self.config.max_provider_failover_attempts
 940        attempt_record["rollback"] = {
 941            "restored": False,
 942            "error": None,
 943            "status": ROLLBACK_PARKED_FOR_GOVERNANCE,
 944            "reason": (
 945                "Candidate preserved for governance instead of being rolled "
 946                "back; no further attempt follows it."
 947            ),
 948        }
 949        attempt_record["next_selection"] = None
 950        attempt_record["next_selection_reason"] = NEXT_SELECTION_MAX_ATTEMPTS
 951        attempt_record["remaining_eligible_resources"] = remaining
 952        attempt_record["transition"] = TRANSITION_CANDIDATE_GOVERNANCE
 953        self._persist_attempt_record(attempt_record, attempts_dir)
 954
 955    @staticmethod
 956    def _recover_implementation_resource(run_dir: Path, routing: Any) -> Optional[str]:
 957        """Restores which resource produced the work being resumed.
 958
 959        A resumed run re-routes from scratch, so the in-memory decision knows
 960        nothing about the failover that already happened. The durable effective
 961        route does, and it is the only truthful source for who to credit --
 962        and, until governance clears it, who not to let review their own work.
 963        """
 964        route_file = run_dir / "effective_route.json"
 965        if route_file.is_file():
 966            try:
 967                meta = (safe_load_json(route_file) or {}).get("metadata") or {}
 968            except Exception:
 969                meta = {}
 970            recovered = (
 971                meta.get("accepted_implementation_resource")
 972                or meta.get("candidate_resource")
 973                or meta.get("last_attempted_implementation_resource")
 974            )
 975            if recovered:
 976                # Carry the failover history forward so this run's evidence
 977                # continues the story instead of restarting it.
 978                for key in (
 979                    "initial_route",
 980                    "initial_implementation_resource",
 981                    "candidate_resource",
 982                    "last_attempted_implementation_resource",
 983                    "reviewer_resource_mapping",
 984                    "reviewer_resource_identities",
 985                ):
 986                    if key in meta and key not in routing.metadata:
 987                        routing.metadata[key] = meta[key]
 988                return recovered
 989        return routing.metadata.get("last_attempted_implementation_resource")
 990
 991    @staticmethod
 992    def _load_parked_candidate(run_dir: Path) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 993        """Recovers a parked timeout candidate's record after an interruption.
 994
 995        The candidate is durable evidence, so a resumed run must know it is
 996        governing a salvaged fragment rather than provider-attested work.
 997        """
 998        attempts_dir = run_dir / "implementation" / "attempts"
 999        if not attempts_dir.is_dir():
1000            return None
1001        for attempt_dir in sorted(attempts_dir.iterdir(), reverse=True):
1002            candidate_file = attempt_dir / "candidate.json"
1003            if candidate_file.is_file():
1004                try:
1005                    return safe_load_json(candidate_file)
1006                except Exception:
1007                    return None
1008        return None
1009
1010    @staticmethod
1011    def _is_salvageable_timeout_candidate(
1012        failure_class: Optional[Any],
1013        delta: Optional[RepositoryDelta],
1014    ) -> bool:
1015        """Reports whether a budget-stopped attempt left work worth governing.
1016
1017        A provider we stopped at our own deadline never claimed completion, but
1018        that says nothing about what it had already written. When such an
1019        attempt leaves a non-empty task-attributable delta, the artifact is a
1020        candidate -- neither trustworthy nor disposable -- and belongs in review
1021        and verification rather than the bin (HOWLFRAM-SLOPFIX-05).
1022        """
1023        if failure_class != ProviderFailureClass.EXECUTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED:
1024            return False
1025        return delta is not None and not delta.is_empty
1026
1027    @staticmethod
1028    def _timed_out_artifact_provenance(
1029        resource_id: str,
1030        attempt: int,
1031        delta: RepositoryDelta,
1032    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1033        """The provenance every budget-stopped artifact carries.
1034
1035        A retained fallback and a governed candidate are the same artifact at
1036        two different points in its life, so they describe their origin
1037        identically -- including the completion claim their producer never made.
1038        """
1039        return {
1040            "provider_completion_claim": False,
1041            "origin": CANDIDATE_ORIGIN_TIMED_OUT,
1042            "failure_class": ProviderFailureClass.EXECUTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.value,
1043            "resource_id": resource_id,
1044            "attempt": attempt,
1045            "files_added": list(delta.files_added),
1046            "files_modified": list(delta.files_modified),
1047            "files_deleted": list(delta.files_deleted),
1048            "insertions": delta.insertions,
1049            "deletions": delta.deletions,
1050            "captured_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
1051        }
1052
1053    def _capture_timeout_candidate(
1054        self,
1055        run_dir: Path,
1056        attempts_dir: Path,
1057        attempt_record: Dict[str, Any],
1058        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1059        resource_id: str,
1060        delta: RepositoryDelta,
1061    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1062        """Preserves a budget-stopped candidate and marks it as needing governance.
1063
1064        Written before any rollback can run, and deliberately separate from the
1065        provider's own result: `implementation/result.json` keeps success=false,
1066        so nothing here fabricates a completion the provider never claimed.
1067        """
1068        candidate = {
1069            "candidate_captured": True,
1070            "requires_governance": True,
1071            **self._timed_out_artifact_provenance(
1072                resource_id, attempt_record["attempt"], delta
1073            ),
1074            "schema": TIMEOUT_CANDIDATE_SCHEMA_VERSION,
1075        }
1076        attempt_dir = attempts_dir / f"{attempt_record['attempt']:02d}-{resource_id}"
1077        attempt_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1078        atomic_write_json(attempt_dir / "candidate.json", candidate)
1079        (attempt_dir / "candidate.patch").write_text(delta.diff_content, encoding="utf-8")
1080
1081        attempt_record["candidate"] = candidate
1082        self._persist_attempt_record(attempt_record, attempts_dir)
1083
1084        # Publish it as the run's current diff so the existing review and
1085        # verification stages act on it exactly as they would a normal one.
1086        self._write_delta_patch(delta, run_dir / "implementation", run_dir)
1087        self._record_event(
1088            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1089            agent_id=resource_id,
1090            action="timeout_candidate_captured",
1091            spec=task_spec,
1092            metadata={
1093                "attempt": attempt_record["attempt"],
1094                "origin": CANDIDATE_ORIGIN_TIMED_OUT,
1095                "provider_completion_claim": False,
1096                "files_changed": len(delta.files_modified) + len(delta.files_added),
1097                "insertions": delta.insertions,
1098                "deletions": delta.deletions,
1099            },
1100        )
1101        return candidate
1102
1103    def _retain_salvage_artifact(
1104        self,
1105        attempts_dir: Path,
1106        attempt_record: Dict[str, Any],
1107        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1108        resource_id: str,
1109        delta: RepositoryDelta,
1110        baseline: GitBaseline,
1111    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1112        """Keeps a productive timeout's work as a bounded terminal fallback.
1113
1114        Rollback must not mean forgetting. HOWLFRAM-SLOPFIX-07R rolled Codex's
1115        eligible EXECUTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED artifact out of the tree so Claude
1116        could attempt from a clean baseline -- which was correct -- and then
1117        terminal-failed without ever reconsidering it, because salvage was only
1118        ever evaluated for whichever attempt happened to be last.
1119
1120        The record lives on the attempt record beside the already-written
1121        partial_work.patch, and deliberately not in a `candidate.json`: while
1122        fresh failover remains this is not the run's candidate and
1123        `candidate_resource` must stay null. Live implementation state and
1124        retained salvageable artifacts are different things.
1125        """
1126        retained = {
1127            "retained": True,
1128            "eligibility": SALVAGE_ELIGIBLE,
1129            "promotion_status": SALVAGE_RETAINED,
1130            **self._timed_out_artifact_provenance(
1131                resource_id, attempt_record["attempt"], delta
1132            ),
1133            "patch_path": f"{attempt_record['evidence_dir']}/retained_salvage.patch",
1134            "patch_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
1135                delta.diff_content.encode("utf-8")
1136            ).hexdigest(),
1137            # Patch identity: what this artifact was captured against, so a
1138            # later promotion can prove it is being replayed onto the same
1139            # repository state rather than whatever happens to be present.
1140            "baseline_head": baseline.initial_commit_sha,
1141            "baseline_status_digest": hashlib.sha256(
1142                baseline.status_porcelain.encode("utf-8")
1143            ).hexdigest(),
1144            # Answered against the restored baseline, which is the only tree
1145            # whose answer means anything. Unknown until rollback has run.
1146            "replayable": None,
1147        }
1148        # Written under a name no attempt-recording path ever produces:
1149        # partial_work.patch belongs to whichever attempt last occupied this
1150        # slot, but the fallback must outlive a resumed re-attempt.
1151        attempt_dir = attempts_dir / f"{attempt_record['attempt']:02d}-{resource_id}"
1152        attempt_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1153        (attempt_dir / "retained_salvage.patch").write_text(
1154            delta.diff_content, encoding="utf-8"
1155        )
1156        attempt_record["retained_salvage"] = retained
1157        self._persist_attempt_record(attempt_record, attempts_dir)
1158        self._record_event(
1159            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1160            agent_id=resource_id,
1161            action="retained_salvage_captured",
1162            spec=task_spec,
1163            metadata={
1164                "attempt": attempt_record["attempt"],
1165                "origin": CANDIDATE_ORIGIN_TIMED_OUT,
1166                "provider_completion_claim": False,
1167                "insertions": delta.insertions,
1168                "deletions": delta.deletions,
1169                "baseline_head": baseline.initial_commit_sha,
1170            },
1171        )
1172        return retained
1173
1174    def _confirm_salvage_replayable(
1175        self,
1176        run_dir: Path,
1177        attempts_dir: Path,
1178        attempt_record: Dict[str, Any],
1179        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1180    ) -> bool:
1181        """Proves the retained patch still applies to the restored baseline.
1182
1183        Deliberately run after rollback rather than before it: the clean
1184        baseline is the tree a promotion would replay onto. `git apply --check`
1185        never writes, so this cannot disturb the state the next provider is
1186        about to be handed. An artifact that fails here stays as evidence but
1187        can never be selected, so it can never be partially applied.
1188        """
1189        retained = attempt_record.get("retained_salvage")
1190        if not retained:
1191            return False
1192        patch_file = run_dir / retained["patch_path"]
1193        replayable = False
1194        if patch_file.is_file():
1195            replayable = run_git(
1196                self.target_repo, ["apply", "--check", str(patch_file)], 60
1197            ).returncode == 0
1198        retained["replayable"] = replayable
1199        if not replayable:
1200            retained["eligibility"] = SALVAGE_NOT_REPLAYABLE
1201        self._persist_attempt_record(attempt_record, attempts_dir)
1202        self._record_event(
1203            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1204            agent_id=retained["resource_id"],
1205            action="retained_salvage_replay_checked",
1206            spec=task_spec,
1207            metadata={
1208                "attempt": retained["attempt"],
1209                "replayable": replayable,
1210                "eligibility": retained["eligibility"],
1211            },
1212        )
1213        return replayable
1214
1215    @staticmethod
1216    def _iter_attempt_records(attempts_dir: Path):
1217        """Yields (record, retained_salvage) per attempt, in attempt order.
1218
1219        Attempt evidence is the durable source of truth for retention, so both
1220        selection and supersession read it from disk rather than from memory --
1221        which is what makes a retained fallback survive an interruption for
1222        free.
1223        """
1224        if not attempts_dir.is_dir():
1225            return
1226        for attempt_dir in sorted(attempts_dir.iterdir()):
1227            record_file = attempt_dir / "attempt_record.json"
1228            if not record_file.is_file():
1229                continue
1230            try:
1231                record = safe_load_json(record_file) or {}
1232            except Exception:
1233                continue
1234            yield record, record.get("retained_salvage") or {}
1235
1236    @staticmethod
1237    def _select_retained_salvage(attempts_dir: Path) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1238        """Picks the fallback deterministically: most recent eligible wins.
1239
1240        No scoring, no ranking, no size heuristic, no model judgment. This
1241        preserves the existing semantics -- a productive *final* timeout is
1242        already the candidate -- and merely extends the search backward to the
1243        nearest prior equivalent when the later attempts produced nothing.
1244
1245        Records are walked in attempt order and the last match is kept, so the
1246        rule holds however many attempts a run is configured to allow.
1247        """
1248        chosen: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
1249        for record, retained in GovernedTaskOrchestrator._iter_attempt_records(
1250            attempts_dir
1251        ):
1252            if (
1253                retained.get("retained")
1254                and retained.get("eligibility") == SALVAGE_ELIGIBLE
1255                and retained.get("promotion_status") == SALVAGE_RETAINED
1256            ):
1257                chosen = record
1258        return chosen
1259
1260    def _recover_promoted_salvage(
1261        self,
1262        run_dir: Path,
1263        delta: RepositoryDelta,
1264        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1265    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1266        """Finishes a promotion that was interrupted after the patch landed.
1267
1268        The crash window between applying a retained patch and capturing the
1269        candidate leaves the artifact sitting in the tree with nothing
1270        describing it. Recovery has to prove the delta in the tree *is* that
1271        artifact, byte for byte, before crediting anyone for it: a resumed run
1272        whose delta came from a later provider -- or from a provider that
1273        simply succeeded -- must not have a rolled-back fragment's producer
1274        stamped onto it. Without that proof this would launder discarded work
1275        into an accepted implementation and certify a self-review as
1276        independent.
1277
1278        Proven, it rebuilds exactly the candidate the uninterrupted path would
1279        have written, so `provider_completion_claim` stays false and the
1280        artifact keeps its timed-out origin.
1281        """
1282        attempts_dir = run_dir / "implementation" / "attempts"
1283        record = self._select_retained_salvage(attempts_dir)
1284        if record is None:
1285            return None
1286        retained = record["retained_salvage"]
1287        if hashlib.sha256(
1288            delta.diff_content.encode("utf-8")
1289        ).hexdigest() != retained.get("patch_sha256"):
1290            return None
1291
1292        candidate = self._capture_timeout_candidate(
1293            run_dir=run_dir,
1294            attempts_dir=attempts_dir,
1295            attempt_record=record,
1296            task_spec=task_spec,
1297            resource_id=retained["resource_id"],
1298            delta=delta,
1299        )
1300        retained["promotion_status"] = SALVAGE_PROMOTED
1301        retained["promoted_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
1302        record["transition"] = TRANSITION_CANDIDATE_GOVERNANCE
1303        self._persist_attempt_record(record, attempts_dir)
1304        self._record_event(
1305            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1306            agent_id=retained["resource_id"],
1307            action="retained_salvage_promotion_recovered",
1308            spec=task_spec,
1309            metadata={
1310                "attempt": retained["attempt"],
1311                "resource_id": retained["resource_id"],
1312                "provider_completion_claim": False,
1313            },
1314        )
1315        return candidate
1316
1317    def _supersede_retained_salvage(
1318        self,
1319        attempts_dir: Path,
1320        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1321    ) -> None:
1322        """Retires every retained fallback once an attempt genuinely succeeds.
1323
1324        Provider-attested work outranks any fragment, so the fallbacks stop
1325        being options the moment one lands. Leaving them selectable would let a
1326        later resume reach for work that was deliberately superseded.
1327        """
1328        for record, retained in self._iter_attempt_records(attempts_dir):
1329            if retained.get("promotion_status") != SALVAGE_RETAINED:
1330                continue
1331            retained["promotion_status"] = SALVAGE_SUPERSEDED
1332            self._persist_attempt_record(record, attempts_dir)
1333            self._record_event(
1334                task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1335                agent_id=retained.get("resource_id", "control_plane"),
1336                action="retained_salvage_superseded",
1337                spec=task_spec,
1338                metadata={"attempt": retained.get("attempt")},
1339            )
1340
1341    def _abandon_salvage_promotion(
1342        self,
1343        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1344        record: Dict[str, Any],
1345        attempts_dir: Path,
1346        reason: str,
1347    ) -> None:
1348        """Retires a fallback that was found but cannot be safely restored.
1349
1350        Marked unusable rather than merely logged: an artifact left eligible
1351        would be re-selected by every subsequent resume, retrying a restore
1352        that has already been proven impossible.
1353        """
1354        retained = record["retained_salvage"]
1355        retained["eligibility"] = SALVAGE_UNUSABLE
1356        retained["abandoned_reason"] = reason
1357        self._persist_attempt_record(record, attempts_dir)
1358        self._record_event(
1359            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1360            agent_id="control_plane",
1361            action="retained_salvage_promotion_failed",
1362            spec=task_spec,
1363            metadata={
1364                "attempt": retained.get("attempt"),
1365                "resource_id": retained.get("resource_id"),
1366                "reason": reason,
1367            },
1368        )
1369
1370    def _promote_retained_salvage(
1371        self,
1372        run_dir: Path,
1373        attempts_dir: Path,
1374        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1375        baseline: GitBaseline,
1376        current_delta: RepositoryDelta,
1377        attempt_record: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
1378    ) -> Optional[Tuple[Dict[str, Any], str, RepositoryDelta]]:
1379        """Recovers the retained fallback once no attempt produced a result.
1380
1381        This is governance of an artifact that already exists, not a new
1382        implementation attempt: no provider is re-invoked, no attempt record is
1383        added, and the bounded failover budget is untouched. Promoting Codex's
1384        retained artifact after attempt 3 failed does not create attempt 4.
1385
1386        Every step fails closed. A fallback that cannot be proven to belong to
1387        this baseline is left as evidence rather than applied, and nothing is
1388        ever partially applied.
1389        """
1390        record = self._select_retained_salvage(attempts_dir)
1391        if record is None:
1392            return None
1393        # `record` is a snapshot read from disk. When the attempt that just
1394        # failed occupies the same evidence slot -- which a resumed run makes
1395        # ordinary, since routing is deterministic -- `attempt_record` is the
1396        # live view of that same file, and writing the snapshot back would
1397        # erase the rollback result recorded below it.
1398        if (
1399            attempt_record is not None
1400            and attempt_record.get("attempt") == record.get("attempt")
1401            and attempt_record.get("resource_id") == record.get("resource_id")
1402        ):
1403            attempt_record["retained_salvage"] = record["retained_salvage"]
1404            record = attempt_record
1405        retained = record["retained_salvage"]
1406        producer = retained["resource_id"]
1407
1408        # The last attempt's state goes back through the sanctioned restore
1409        # path first, so pre-existing user work is put back before anything is
1410        # applied on top of it.
1411        restored_ok, restore_err = restore_repository_to_baseline(
1412            self.target_repo, baseline, current_delta
1413        )
1414        # The attempt that just failed still owes an honest rollback record.
1415        # Its work was undone here rather than in the failover branch, and
1416        # evidence that goes silent about it is what SLOPFIX-06 fixed.
1417        if attempt_record is not None:
1418            self._attach_rollback_result(
1419                attempt_record, attempts_dir, restored_ok, restore_err
1420            )
1421        if not restored_ok:
1422            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1423                task_spec, record, attempts_dir, f"baseline restore failed: {restore_err}"
1424            )
1425            return None
1426
1427        head_proc = run_git(self.target_repo, ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], 30)
1428        head = head_proc.stdout.strip() if head_proc.returncode == 0 else ""
1429        if head != retained.get("baseline_head"):
1430            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1431                task_spec,
1432                record,
1433                attempts_dir,
1434                f"baseline HEAD mismatch: expected {retained.get('baseline_head')}, "
1435                f"got {head or 'unknown'}",
1436            )
1437            return None
1438
1439        if hashlib.sha256(
1440            baseline.status_porcelain.encode("utf-8")
1441        ).hexdigest() != retained.get("baseline_status_digest"):
1442            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1443                task_spec,
1444                record,
1445                attempts_dir,
1446                "baseline state digest does not match the one captured with "
1447                "the artifact",
1448            )
1449            return None
1450
1451        patch_file = run_dir / retained["patch_path"]
1452        if not patch_file.is_file():
1453            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1454                task_spec, record, attempts_dir, f"retained patch missing at {retained['patch_path']}"
1455            )
1456            return None
1457        patch_text = patch_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
1458        if hashlib.sha256(patch_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() != retained.get(
1459            "patch_sha256"
1460        ):
1461            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1462                task_spec, record, attempts_dir, "retained patch digest does not match its record"
1463            )
1464            return None
1465
1466        # Never `git apply` blind. Prove it applies, then apply it.
1467        if run_git(
1468            self.target_repo, ["apply", "--check", str(patch_file)], 60
1469        ).returncode != 0:
1470            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1471                task_spec, record, attempts_dir, "retained patch no longer applies to the baseline"
1472            )
1473            return None
1474        applied = run_git(self.target_repo, ["apply", str(patch_file)], 60)
1475        if applied.returncode != 0:
1476            restore_repository_to_baseline(self.target_repo, baseline)
1477            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1478                task_spec,
1479                record,
1480                attempts_dir,
1481                f"retained patch failed to apply: {(applied.stderr or '').strip()}",
1482            )
1483            return None
1484
1485        self._fault(FAULT_DURING_SALVAGE_PROMOTION, run_dir, task_spec)
1486
1487        promoted_delta = self._capture_scoped_delta(
1488            task_spec, baseline, producer, stage="salvage_promotion"
1489        )
1490        if promoted_delta.is_empty:
1491            restore_repository_to_baseline(self.target_repo, baseline)
1492            self._abandon_salvage_promotion(
1493                task_spec, record, attempts_dir, "restored artifact produced no task-attributable delta"
1494            )
1495            return None
1496
1497        # From here the artifact is an ordinary governed candidate: the same
1498        # capture the existing terminal-timeout path uses, with the same
1499        # provider_completion_claim=false, entering the same review,
1500        # verification and authority stages.
1501        candidate = self._capture_timeout_candidate(
1502            run_dir=run_dir,
1503            attempts_dir=attempts_dir,
1504            attempt_record=record,
1505            task_spec=task_spec,
1506            resource_id=producer,
1507            delta=promoted_delta,
1508        )
1509        retained["promotion_status"] = SALVAGE_PROMOTED
1510        retained["promoted_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
1511        record["transition"] = TRANSITION_CANDIDATE_GOVERNANCE
1512        self._persist_attempt_record(record, attempts_dir)
1513        # The attempt that ended the chain says so on its own record, rather
1514        # than leaving "an earlier fallback was governed instead" recoverable
1515        # only from the ledger.
1516        if attempt_record is not None and attempt_record is not record:
1517            attempt_record["next_selection"] = None
1518            attempt_record["next_selection_reason"] = (
1519                NEXT_SELECTION_SALVAGE_PROMOTED
1520            )
1521            attempt_record["transition"] = TRANSITION_CANDIDATE_GOVERNANCE
1522            self._persist_attempt_record(attempt_record, attempts_dir)
1523        self._record_event(
1524            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1525            agent_id=producer,
1526            action="retained_salvage_promoted",
1527            spec=task_spec,
1528            metadata={
1529                "attempt": retained["attempt"],
1530                "resource_id": producer,
1531                "provider_completion_claim": False,
1532                "insertions": promoted_delta.insertions,
1533                "deletions": promoted_delta.deletions,
1534                "baseline_head": retained["baseline_head"],
1535            },
1536        )
1537        return candidate, producer, promoted_delta
1538
1539    def _build_failover_summary(
1540        self,
1541        implementation_attempts: List[Dict[str, Any]],
1542        termination_reason: str,
1543        last_decision: Any,
1544    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1545        """Explains exhaustion so an operator never has to guess why it stopped."""
1546        remaining: List[str] = []
1547        excluded: Dict[str, str] = {}
1548        if last_decision is not None:
1549            selected = getattr(last_decision, "selected", None)
1550            remaining = [
1551                identity.resource_id
1552                for identity in getattr(last_decision, "eligible_resources", []) or []
1553                if selected is None or identity.resource_id != selected.resource_id
1554            ]
1555            excluded = {
1556                exclusion.resource_id: exclusion.reason
1557                for exclusion in getattr(last_decision, "exclusions", []) or []
1558            }
1559        return {
1560            "attempts_used": len(implementation_attempts),
1561            "attempts_allowed": self.config.max_provider_failover_attempts,
1562            "termination_reason": termination_reason,
1563            "attempted_resources": [
1564                {
1565                    "attempt": attempt.get("attempt"),
1566                    "resource_id": attempt.get("resource_id"),
1567                    "failure_class": attempt.get("failure_class"),
1568                }
1569                for attempt in implementation_attempts
1570            ],
1571            "remaining_eligible": remaining,
1572            "excluded": excluded,
1573            "schema": FAILOVER_SUMMARY_SCHEMA_VERSION,
1574        }
1575
1576    def _is_failover_eligible_failure(self, failure_class: Optional[Any]) -> bool:
1577        """Returns True when the normalized failure class justifies provider failover."""
1578        if failure_class is None:
1579            return False
1580        return failure_class in {
1581            ProviderFailureClass.QUOTA_EXHAUSTED,
1582            ProviderFailureClass.SESSION_LIMIT,
1583            ProviderFailureClass.RATE_LIMITED,
1584            ProviderFailureClass.AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED,
1585            ProviderFailureClass.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE,
1586            ProviderFailureClass.TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE,
1587            ProviderFailureClass.EXECUTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED,
1588            ProviderFailureClass.MISSING_EXECUTABLE,
1589            ProviderFailureClass.EXECUTION_PERMISSION_REQUIRED,
1590        }
1591
1592    def _map_failure_class_to_orchestrator_class(
1593        self,
1594        failure_class: Optional[Any],
1595    ) -> str:
1596        """Maps a provider failure class to the orchestrator's coarse failure class."""
1597        if failure_class is None:
1598            return FAILURE_CLASS_ENGINEERING
1599        value = getattr(failure_class, "value", str(failure_class))
1600        if value in {"QUOTA_EXHAUSTED", "SESSION_LIMIT", "RATE_LIMITED"}:
1601            return FAILURE_CLASS_PROVIDER_EXHAUSTED
1602        if value == "EXECUTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED":
1603            return FAILURE_CLASS_EXECUTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
1604        if value in {
1605            "AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED",
1606            "PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE",
1607            "TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE",
1608            "MISSING_EXECUTABLE",
1609            "EXECUTION_PERMISSION_REQUIRED",
1610        }:
1611            return FAILURE_CLASS_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE
1612        return FAILURE_CLASS_ENGINEERING
1613
1614    def run_deterministic_verification(
1615        self,
1616        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1617        run_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
1618        progress: Optional[Any] = None,
1619        verif_plan: Optional[VerificationPlan] = None,
1620        baseline: Optional[GitBaseline] = None,
1621        delta: Optional[RepositoryDelta] = None,
1622    ) -> str:
1623        """Executes the deterministic verification plan for settled work.
1624
1625        The Stage 6 gate is reachable only by running the whole loop from the
1626        top, which re-invokes providers. A task that escalated to
1627        `awaiting_human` before Stage 6 already has its implementation, its
1628        reviews and its plan on disk; what it never had was the gate. This runs
1629        exactly that gate against the same sanitized view Stage 6 uses, and
1630        persists the same evidence.
1631
1632        Idempotent: a plan whose `overall_status` is already terminal is
1633        returned unchanged rather than re-executed, so a repeated resume cannot
1634        turn a recorded failure into a fresh pass (issues.md #12).
1635
1636        Returns the plan's overall status. Never transitions the task to
1637        `complete` -- that is the caller's policy decision.
1638        """
1639        run_dir = run_dir or (self.target_repo / ".task_runs" / task_spec.task_id)
1640        if verif_plan is None:
1641            plan_file = run_dir / "verification_plan.json"
1642            if not plan_file.is_file():
1643                raise VerificationPlanMissingError(
1644                    f"Task '{task_spec.task_id}' has no verification_plan.json at "
1645                    f"{plan_file}. Deterministic verification cannot be claimed "
1646                    f"for a plan that does not exist."
1647                )
1648            verif_plan = VerificationPlan.from_dict(safe_load_json(plan_file))
1649            if verif_plan.overall_status in TERMINAL_VERIFICATION_STATUSES:
1650                return verif_plan.overall_status
1651
1652        if baseline is None:
1653            baseline_file = run_dir / "baseline.json"
1654            if baseline_file.is_file():
1655                baseline = GitBaseline.from_dict(safe_load_json(baseline_file))
1656            else:
1657                baseline = capture_baseline(self.target_repo)
1658        if delta is None:
1659            delta = capture_delta(self.target_repo, baseline)
1660
1661        CheckpointManager.start_stage(
1662            run_dir,
1663            task_spec.task_id,
1664            "verifying",
1665            repo_path=self.target_repo,
1666            input_artifacts=[str(run_dir / "diff.patch")],
1667        )
1668        if task_spec.current_state != "verifying":
1669            task_spec.transition_to(
1670                "verifying",
1671                "Human approval authorized the governed workflow to continue; "
1672                "executing the deterministic verification plan that the "
1673                "pre-verification escalation skipped.",
1674            )
1675            task_spec.save_to_file(str(run_dir / "task.yaml"))
1676
1677        self._record_event(
1678            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1679            agent_id="control_plane",
1680            action="verification_started",
1681            spec=task_spec,
1682            metadata={
1683                "steps_count": len(verif_plan.steps),
1684                "trigger": "resume_after_pre_verification_escalation",
1685            },
1686        )
1687
1688        verif_status = self._execute_verification_plan(
1689            verif_plan=verif_plan,
1690            task_spec=task_spec,
1691            baseline=baseline,
1692            delta=delta,
1693            run_dir=run_dir,
1694            progress=progress,
1695        )
1696
1697        plan_json = verif_plan.to_json()
1698        (run_dir / "verification_plan.json").write_text(plan_json, encoding="utf-8")
1699        (run_dir / "verification_result.json").write_text(plan_json, encoding="utf-8")
1700
1701        self._record_event(
1702            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1703            agent_id="control_plane",
1704            action="verification_completed",
1705            spec=task_spec,
1706            result=verif_status,
1707            verification_summary={s.name: s.status for s in verif_plan.steps},
1708        )
1709        CheckpointManager.complete_stage(
1710            run_dir,
1711            "verifying",
1712            output_artifacts=[str(run_dir / "verification_result.json")],
1713            result_summary={s.name: s.status for s in verif_plan.steps},
1714        )
1715        return verif_status
1716
1717    def _set_effective_implementer(
1718        self,
1719        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1720        run_dir: Path,
1721        resource_id: Optional[str],
1722    ) -> None:
1723        """Pins the single authoritative effective-implementer identity.
1724
1725        `actual_agent` mirrors it so durable task metadata, the
1726        reviewer-independence records (which read the same resource id) and the
1727        final summary cannot disagree about who produced the governed
1728        candidate. Full attempt history is untouched -- every provider that was
1729        asked still has its own record under implementation/attempts/.
1730
1731        A no-op when implementation produced no resource at all, so a task that
1732        failed before any provider ran does not claim an implementer
1733        (issues.md #16).
1734        """
1735        if not resource_id:
1736            return
1737        task_spec.effective_implementer_resource_id = resource_id
1738        task_spec.actual_agent = resource_id
1739        # The dispatch slot is per-invocation scratch; it must not survive as a
1740        # second, contradictory answer to "who implemented this".
1741        task_spec.dispatch_resource_id = None
1742        task_spec.save_to_file(str(run_dir / "task.yaml"))
1743
1744    def _persist_effective_route(
1745        self,
1746        routing: Any,
1747        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1748        attempt_resource_id: str,
1749        route_status: str,
1750        accepted: bool,
1751        candidate_resource: Optional[str] = None,
1752        last_attempted_resource_id: Optional[str] = None,
1753    ) -> None:
1754        """Makes routing evidence on disk match who is actually implementing.
1755
1756        This used to run only after a *successful* failover, so a run that
1757        failed over and then failed left route.json still naming the originally
1758        routed provider, with no effective_route.json at all -- durable evidence
1759        contradicting the run (HOWLFRAM-SLOPFIX-05). Routing becomes durable at
1760        every real handoff instead, and distinguishes the resource currently
1761        attempting implementation from one whose work was actually accepted.
1762
1763        initial_route.json is never touched here; it stays the immutable record
1764        of what was routed first.
1765        """
1766        if self.config.provider_pool is None:
1767            return
1768        if "initial_route" not in routing.metadata:
1769            routing.metadata["initial_route"] = {
1770                "selected_agent_id": routing.selected_agent_id,
1771                "selected_agent_name": getattr(
1772                    routing, "selected_agent_name", routing.selected_agent_id
1773                ),
1774                "reviewer_resource_mapping": dict(
1775                    routing.metadata.get("reviewer_resource_mapping", {})
1776                ),
1777                "reviewer_resource_identities": dict(
1778                    routing.metadata.get("reviewer_resource_identities", {})
1779                ),
1780                "review_diversity_achieved": routing.metadata.get(
1781                    "review_diversity_achieved"
1782                ),
1783            }
1784
1785        # Reviewers are recomputed against whoever is implementing now, so no
1786        # mapping can imply a provider reviews its own work. Until a candidate
1787        # is actually accepted the mapping is labelled provisional, because the
1788        # implementer may change again on the next hop.
1789        mapping, diversity = self.config.provider_pool.select_reviewers(
1790            attempt_resource_id,
1791            routing.recommended_reviewers,
1792            task=task_spec,
1793        )
1794        registry = self.config.provider_pool.registry
1795        identities = {
1796            role: registry.get_resource(resource_id).resource_identity().to_dict()
1797            for role, resource_id in mapping.items()
1798            if registry.get_resource(resource_id) is not None
1799        }
1800        routing.metadata["reviewer_resource_mapping"] = mapping
1801        routing.metadata["reviewer_resource_identities"] = identities
1802        routing.metadata["review_diversity_achieved"] = diversity
1803        routing.metadata["reviewer_mapping_status"] = (
1804            "CONFIRMED"
1805            if accepted
1806            else ("CANDIDATE_REVIEW" if candidate_resource else "PROVISIONAL")
1807        )
1808        routing.metadata["route_status"] = route_status
1809        # Promoting a retained fallback credits the resource that produced the
1810        # artifact, but the last resource that actually *ran* is still the one
1811        # the failover chain ended on. Conflating them would rewrite history as
1812        # though the producer had been the final implementation attempt.
1813        routing.metadata["current_attempt_resource"] = (
1814            last_attempted_resource_id or attempt_resource_id
1815        )
1816        routing.metadata["last_attempted_implementation_resource"] = (
1817            last_attempted_resource_id or attempt_resource_id
1818        )
1819        routing.metadata["initial_implementation_resource"] = (
1820            routing.metadata.get("initial_route", {}).get("selected_agent_id")
1821            or routing.selected_agent_id
1822        )
1823        # A candidate is work that exists and is being governed; an accepted
1824        # implementation is work that cleared review, verification and
1825        # authority. Conflating them let SLOPFIX-06's route evidence claim an
1826        # accepted implementer while the task was still under review.
1827        routing.metadata["candidate_resource"] = candidate_resource
1828        routing.metadata["accepted_implementation_resource"] = (
1829            attempt_resource_id if accepted else None
1830        )
1831        routing.metadata["final_implementation_resource"] = (
1832            attempt_resource_id if accepted else None
1833        )
1834        routing.metadata["final_route"] = {
1835            "selected_agent_id": attempt_resource_id,
1836            "accepted": accepted,
1837            "reviewer_resource_mapping": mapping,
1838            "reviewer_resource_identities": identities,
1839            "review_diversity_achieved": diversity,
1840        }
1841        routing.metadata["reassignment_reason"] = (
1842            f"Implementation moved from {routing.selected_agent_id} to "
1843            f"{attempt_resource_id}; reviewers recomputed to keep review "
1844            f"independent of the implementer"
1845        )
1846
1847        # The effective implementer as durable routing evidence, so
1848        # effective_route.json, task.yaml and the summary answer the question
1849        # from one value rather than three (issues.md #16).
1850        routing.metadata["effective_implementer_resource_id"] = attempt_resource_id
1851
1852        run_dir = self.target_repo / ".task_runs" / task_spec.task_id
1853        if run_dir.exists():
1854            atomic_write_json(run_dir / "route.json", asdict(routing))
1855            effective = asdict(routing)
1856            effective["selected_agent_id"] = attempt_resource_id
1857            # The name has to follow the id. HOWLFRAM-BUG-52's
1858            # effective_route.json read `selected_agent_id: claude_code` beside
1859            # `selected_agent_name: "Antigravity CLI (agy)"` because only the id
1860            # was rewritten here, leaving the originally routed provider's name
1861            # attached to a different resource.
1862            effective_profile = registry.get_resource(attempt_resource_id)
1863            if effective_profile is not None:
1864                effective["selected_agent_name"] = getattr(
1865                    effective_profile, "name", attempt_resource_id
1866                )
1867            else:
1868                effective["selected_agent_name"] = attempt_resource_id
1869            atomic_write_json(run_dir / "effective_route.json", effective)
1870
1871        self._record_event(
1872            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1873            agent_id="control_plane",
1874            action="effective_route_updated",
1875            spec=task_spec,
1876            metadata={
1877                "initial_implementation_resource": routing.selected_agent_id,
1878                "attempt_resource": attempt_resource_id,
1879                "candidate_resource": candidate_resource,
1880                "accepted_implementation_resource": (
1881                    attempt_resource_id if accepted else None
1882                ),
1883                "route_status": route_status,
1884                "reviewer_mapping": mapping,
1885                "diversity_achieved": diversity,
1886            },
1887        )
1888
1889    def _record_event(
1890        self,
1891        task_id: str,
1892        agent_id: str,
1893        action: str,
1894        command: Optional[str] = None,
1895        result: Optional[str] = None,
1896        artifact: Optional[str] = None,
1897        spec: Optional[TaskSpec] = None,
1898        findings_summary: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None,
1899        verification_summary: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
1900        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
1901    ) -> None:
1902        """Records an immutable event in the append-only evidence ledger."""
1903        if not self.config.record_evidence:
1904            return
1905
1906        meta = metadata or {}
1907        entry = EvidenceEntry(
1908            task_id=task_id,
1909            agent_id=agent_id,
1910            action=action,
1911            command=command,
1912            result=result,
1913            artifact=artifact,
1914            task_class=spec.task_class if spec else None,
1915            risk_level=spec.risk_level if spec else None,
1916            reasoning_tier=spec.recommended_reasoning_tier if spec else None,
1917            actual_agent=agent_id,
1918            repository=self.target_repo.name,
1919            findings_summary=findings_summary,
1920            verification_summary=verification_summary,
1921            metadata=meta,
1922        )
1923        try:
1924            self.ledger.append_entry(entry)
1925        except Exception:
1926            pass
1927
1928    def _write_delta_patch(
1929        self,
1930        delta: RepositoryDelta,
1931        stage_dir: Path,
1932        run_dir: Path,
1933    ) -> None:
1934        """Publishes a captured patch as the stage artifact and the run's current diff."""
1935        (stage_dir / "diff.patch").write_text(delta.diff_content, encoding="utf-8")
1936        (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text(delta.diff_content, encoding="utf-8")
1937
1938    def _record_delta_captured(
1939        self,
1940        task_spec: TaskSpec,
1941        delta: Optional[RepositoryDelta] = None,
1942    ) -> None:
1943        """Records the repository_delta_captured event for a captured delta."""
1944        self._record_event(
1945            task_id=task_spec.task_id,
1946            agent_id="control_plane",
1947            action="repository_delta_captured",
1948            spec=task_spec,
1949            metadata=delta.to_event_metadata() if delta is not None else None,
1950        )
